title: A Claude turn begun by a background-task notification gets no turn record, so its edits never become mutations
outcome: A Claude turn begun by a background-task notification gets no turn record, so its edits never become mutations
acceptance: A Claude Code turn that the runtime starts by itself after a background-task notice has no proven pre-effect runtime boundary (Termal::Opus2's live probes of 2026-10-02 and Architect2's note 2e8c540c: the runtime begins it without a host prompt, so the host can detect it only after it has started). It is therefore never admitted, retroactively or otherwise (no turn_evaluate, turn_begin or checkpoint for it), and in a session bound to claimed work it is recorded through Engram's execution_observe as an unadmitted_turn. In a session with no claimed work binding it reports nothing to Engram, and the host's transcript notice for the turn says so.

Continuity drift that the host detects between two checkpoints of the same workspace and run reaches the Engram store through the producer representation agreed with Engram, so a checkpoint whose turn reports source_changed=false travels with that explanation; a test shows it.

A source edit or test run in a runtime-started turn reaches the store either as granted evidence of a mediated turn or as observed, uncredited evidence of a detected turn, and never as credit under another turn's grant; a test shows both.
